content.text:
1) Answer

Short proof, using verifiable actions, decisions, and statements:

- Long-standing work to reduce discrimination in the justice system: He led the government‑commissioned Lammy Review (published 8 September 2017), which set out 35 recommendations to increase fairness, transparency and equal treatment for Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic people in England and Wales’ criminal justice system. That body of work is evidence of sustained human‑rights‑oriented values in practice. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/lammy-review-final-report?utm_source=openai))

- Direct support for human rights defenders: As Foreign Secretary, on Human Rights Day (10 December 2024), he sent formal letters of solidarity to imprisoned and at‑risk activists (e.g., Ales Bialiatski in Belarus; Pastor Lorenzo in Cuba; Angie Zapata in Colombia) and publicly stated “the protection of fundamental freedoms is vital.” This is an explicit, documented commitment to human rights. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-foreign-secretary-backs-human-rights-defenders-on-human-rights-day?utm_source=openai))

- Making human rights central to UK positions at the UN: In national statements and speeches (23 September 2024; 25 September 2025), he framed UK foreign policy around the UN Charter, rule of law and universal rights, calling for “responsible global leadership” and consistency in upholding rights. These are official transcripts of his words. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/a-reformed-multilateral-system-is-the-path-to-peace-and-prosperity-on-a-livable-planet-foreign-secretary-speech-at-the-un-summit-of-the-future?utm_source=openai))

- Advancing international accountability: On 9 May 2025 in Lviv, he outlined UK support for a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine, arguing for accountability under international law—core human‑rights architecture. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/foreign-secretary-speech-in-lviv-on-the-special-tribunal?utm_source=openai))

- Acting against abuses and protecting civilians: On 22 July 2025, he condemned actions in Gaza that harmed starving civilians and said the UK would escalate sanctions if necessary—using state tools to seek compliance with humanitarian law and protect life. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2025/jul/22/lammy-israel-sanctions-for-targeting-starving-palestinians?utm_source=openai))

- Embedding human rights and the rule of law at home: On becoming Lord Chancellor (1 October 2025), he pledged “to defend those values [rights and the rule of law] at home, and overseas,” emphasizing equality before the law—again, an official text of record. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/lord-chancellor-swearing-in-speech-rt-hon-david-lammy-mp?utm_source=openai))

- Recognizing indigenous rights and environmental defenders: At COP29 (12 November 2024) he highlighted the role and protection of Indigenous Peoples and local communities in safeguarding nature—rights language tied to climate and land stewardship. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/foreign-secretarys-speech-on-indigenous-peoples-and-protecting-forests?utm_source=openai))

- Commissioning independent scrutiny in a rights‑sensitive case: As Foreign Secretary he ordered an independent review (7 July 2025) into the government’s handling of the Harry Dunn case—an accountability step to improve how the state supports UK citizens’ rights after serious harm abroad. ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/review-into-government-response-to-the-death-of-harry-dunn?utm_source=openai))

Taken together—decade‑long equality work in justice, public advocacy for rights defenders, UN‑anchored rule‑of‑law rhetoric, concrete accountability measures, and formal pledges as Lord Chancellor—constitute strong evidence that David Lammy values human rights.

- GOV.UK (official UK government pages: FCDO, MoJ, No10)

(Cited items: UN Summit of the Future statement 23 Sep 2024; UNGA national statement 25 Sep 2025; Lviv Special Tribunal speech 9 May 2025; Human Rights Day letters 11 Dec 2024; Lord Chancellor swearing‑in speech 1 Oct 2025; COP29 Indigenous speech 12 Nov 2024; Harry Dunn review announcement 7 Jul 2025; ministerial appointments 5 Sep 2025.) ([gov.uk](https://www.gov.uk/government/speeches/a-reformed-multilateral-system-is-the-path-to-peace-and-prosperity-on-a-livable-planet-foreign-secretary-speech-at-the-un-summit-of-the-future?utm_source=openai))

  [3] Reasoning 2: Confirms Lammy’s current roles and provides documentary record relevant to human‑rights‑related policy oversight. (Example used: Justice and Home Affairs Committee correspondence, 30 Sep 2025.) ([api.parliament.uk](https://api.parliament.uk/committees/publications/49722?utm_source=openai))

  [3] Reasoning 2: Provided contemporaneous reporting of Lammy’s Gaza statements and threatened sanctions—useful independent corroboration of an official stance on a live humanitarian crisis.
